## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vinīlajātaka* (Ja 160) is a story included in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework, the Buddha related this story while residing at Veḷuvana regarding Devadatta's imitation of the Buddha [SuttaCentral].

In the story of the past, during the reign of the Bodhisatta as king of Mithilā in the Videha country, a golden goose king (*suvaṇṇarājahamsa*) mated with a crow (*kākī*) [Fausböll 1879]. Their hybrid offspring, being neither like its mother nor its father and exhibiting a livid or dark blue hue (*vinīlakadhātukattā*), was named Vinīlaka [Fausböll 1879]. In the narrative's verses and commentary, Vinīlaka is rebuked for overstepping his station and attempting to frequent realms unsuited to him, being instructed instead to haunt village outskirts, the natural habitat of his maternal kin (*Vinīla, duggaṁ bhajasi, abhūmiṁ tāta sevasi...*) [Fausböll 1879]. In the concluding identification, Vinīla represents Devadatta [Fausböll 1897].

SuttaCentral lists four translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any Pali-internal text reuse matches or cross-language parallels for this text [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
